claims.text: 4th Street & Harrison Street had 28 injury crashes in police records since 2021-10-31: 0 people killed.
These counts are 4th Street & Harrison Street's own: the city's record places 10 of the 38 records within 100 m at another intersection or street, and they are left out.
At the U.S. DOT's values that harm costs about $1.9 million a year.
No crash pattern here stands out against the city's worst crash locations.

This corner got continental crosswalks in 2020. Across the city: at 780 sites the change in pedestrian injury crashes (+4%, 95% interval -25% to +33%) could be zero. The city's own record neither shows it worked nor rules it out, so repeating it here rests on other evidence.
The city's painted safety zones: not shown (at 96 sites the change in pedestrian injury crashes (+2%, 95% interval -20% to +34%) could be zero); a second run of the same design on 780 sites agrees.
Leading Pedestrian Interval would avoid about 0.1 crashes a year (CMF 9918, the record FHWA's fact sheet cites; evidence: the record FHWA cites), worth $36,000 a year.

Backplates with Retroreflective Borders would avoid about 0.8 crashes a year (CMF 1410, the record FHWA's fact sheet cites; evidence: only if a site check confirms it), worth $288,000 a year; check on site: an entry on yellow or red.

The San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency (SFMTA) is responsible for 4th Street, Clara Street, Harrison Street, Perry Street, Rizal Street, Tandang Sora Street (no route reference, so presumed a city street).
A request letter to the San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency (SFMTA) is ready to draft from these facts.
